html:
SMTO-EXE-0261 — A saved account or private value this workflow needs is missing

GUID: cc925822-b014-577c-a069-9ee8286a14fb
Slug: recipe-secret-reference-missing
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: recipes

What happened

  • This workflow refers to an entry in the Parameter Store, where SMTO keeps passwords and other private values, but that entry can't be found or its name is written wrong. SMTO stopped before running the workflow's steps.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Parameter Store and search for the entry the workflow uses, such as the account it signs in with. The workflow looks the entry up by its exact name, so a renamed or deleted entry can't be found.
  2. If the entry is missing, add it again with exactly the same name. If it was renamed, change the name back. Restoring the exact name lets the workflow find it without changing the workflow.
  3. If you can't tell which name it needs, save the request again with Save to workflow and refer to the entry by typing @ followed by its current name. A new save points the workflow at an entry that exists now.

What success looks like

  • The workflow gets past this point and its task starts without this message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't type the password or key directly into the workflow to get around this; SMTO will block it.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A reference-only workflow value has invalid @reference syntax, or a required @reference does not resolve exactly in the current Parameter Store.

What this means

  • A reference-only value has invalid @reference syntax, or a required reference cannot be resolved exactly through the current Parameter Store. Workflow diagnostics do not execute steps or grant approval. Preserve the pinned definition, original receipts, completed effects and any uncertainty; all execution uses the existing authorization boundary.

Why this can happen

  • A reference-only value has invalid @reference syntax, or a required reference cannot be resolved exactly through the current Parameter Store.

How to diagnose it

  • Check reference syntax, exact record existence and availability of the Parameter Store; do not substitute a credential literal.

How to fix it

  • List the workflow's required_parameter_refs and reference-only parameter values, then check parameter_store.get_exact for each name (validation.parameters, validation.revalidate). Restore the exact key, or correct the value to the @name form (an @ followed by a letter or digit, then up to 159 letters, digits, dots, dashes or underscores).
  • Select or restore the exact required Parameter Store reference and validate the invocation again.

Retry and execution caution

  • Review the workflow and its current run evidence before retrying.

How to verify the fix

  • Every required reference resolves privately through the accepted invocation context.

What not to do

  • Never repeat a write whose effect remains unknown.

Technical notes

  • Workflow diagnostics do not execute steps or grant approval. Preserve the pinned definition, original receipts, completed effects and any uncertainty; all execution uses the existing authorization boundary.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
